modules.name: Clock
modules.header:
Reading a clock, and waiting on one.
`ClockMonotonic` counts forward from an arbitrary point and never jumps; `ClockRealtime` tracks wall time and can
move in either direction. A duration is measured with the first, a timestamp taken from the second.
FreeBSD numbers its clocks differently from Linux — monotonic is 4 here and 1 there — which is why an identifier
must never be carried between the two packages.

modules.name: Dynamic
modules.header:
Loading a shared object at run time, and finding a symbol inside it.
The one part of the FreeBSD interface that is not a system call: resolution, relocation and reference counting all
belong to the run-time linker, whose entry points live in libc.

modules.name: Entropy
modules.header:
Unpredictable bytes, from the kernel's own generator.
The only source in this package fit for a key, a token, or anything an adversary would like to guess. FreeBSD's
generator is always seeded by the time user code runs, so unlike Linux's there is no first-boot wait to think
about — but a short count is still possible and still has to be looped over.

modules.name: Errors
modules.header:
How a FreeBSD system call reports failure, and the numbers it reports.
FreeBSD does not report an error the way Linux does. The kernel sets the carry flag and leaves a *positive* errno
in the result register, so the raw instruction result cannot be tested for sign. The assembly wrappers in
`Syscall` normalize that to Linux's convention — a small negative number — so everything above them reads the
same on both systems, and `IsError` and `Errno` are then the same two functions.
The names keep the system's own spelling, because `EINVAL` is what a man page names. The values below are
FreeBSD's, which agree with Linux for the first thirty-four and then diverge.

modules.name: File
modules.header:
Reading and writing through a file descriptor, and the three descriptors a process starts with.
Each wrapper returns the normalized raw result: a byte count, or a small negative error number. A short count is
not an error and not an end of file — only a zero-length read means the source has ended.
The three descriptor constants are annotated `int32` rather than `FileDescriptor`, because a `const` cannot name a
type alias declared in another file of the package.

modules.name: Memory
modules.header:
Mapping and unmapping address space, and moving the program break.
Nothing here tracks what it hands out: an address from `Mmap` is valid until `Munmap` releases exactly the range
that was mapped.

modules.name: Process
modules.header:
What a process can ask or say about itself.
Nothing here creates a process: a raw binding to `fork` and `execve` without signal handling, descriptor
inheritance and a wait protocol would be an invitation to get all three wrong.

modules.name: Syscall
modules.header:
The raw system-call entry points, and the numbers that select a call.
Every wrapper elsewhere in this package is one of these seven functions with the arguments named. A caller may use
them directly for a call this package does not wrap, which is what they are public for.
Unlike Linux, both supported architectures share one numbering: FreeBSD assigns a call its number once, in
`syscalls.master`, and every architecture uses it. What differs is only where the number and the arguments go.
A raw result from these wrappers is already normalized to Linux's convention — a value, or a small negative error
number — which is what `Errors::IsError` and `Errors::Errno` read.

modules.name: Types
modules.header:
The kernel ABI's own types: what a FreeBSD system call takes and gives back.
FreeBSD's 64-bit ABI fixes each width, so these are the same on both supported architectures and none of the
`long` questions that `Rux/C` has to answer arise here.

items.name: Nanosleep
items.signature: pub func Nanosleep(request: *Timespec, remaining: *var Timespec) -> int64

doc.summary: Suspends the caller for the requested duration.
doc.markdown:
Suspends the caller for the requested duration.
`remaining` is written when a signal cut the wait short, and may be null. Returns zero, or a negative error
number; `EINTR` with the unslept time in `remaining` is how a signal is reported.
`request` must be non-null, and its nanoseconds must be under one second.

params.name: remaining
params.markdown: receives the unslept time when a signal cut the wait short, and may be null

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.markdown:
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC_FAST`: like `ClockMonotonic`, read from a cached value rather than the hardware.
Cheaper and coarser. FreeBSD offers this pairing where Linux offers a coarse clock under a different number.

items.name: GetRandom
items.signature: pub func GetRandom(buffer: *var opaque, length: uint, flags: uint32) -> int64

doc.summary: Fills up to `length` bytes of `buffer` with unpredictable bytes.
doc.markdown:
Fills up to `length` bytes of `buffer` with unpredictable bytes.
Returns the number of bytes actually written, or a negative error number. A request over 256 bytes may be cut
short, and a caller needing the whole buffer must call again for the rest.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes. Treat a short count as bytes obtained, not as failure, or the
unwritten tail stays whatever it held — which for a key is the worst possible outcome.

params.name: length
params.markdown: how many bytes to ask for

params.name: flags
params.markdown: zero, or one of the `Random*` values

doc.returns: the bytes written, which may be fewer than asked for, or a negative error number

items.name: Read
items.signature: pub func Read(fd: FileDescriptor, buffer: *var opaque, count: uint) -> int64

doc.summary: Reads up to `count` bytes from `fd` into `buffer`.
doc.markdown:
Reads up to `count` bytes from `fd` into `buffer`.
`buffer` is borrowed and written. Returns the number of bytes read, zero at end of file, or a negative error
number. A short count is ordinary.
`buffer` must be writable for `count` bytes.

params.name: count
params.markdown: how many bytes to ask for

doc.returns: the bytes read, zero at end of file, or a negative error number

items.name: Write
items.signature: pub func Write(fd: FileDescriptor, buffer: *opaque, count: uint) -> int64

doc.summary: Writes up to `count` bytes from `buffer` to `fd`.
doc.markdown:
Writes up to `count` bytes from `buffer` to `fd`.
`buffer` is borrowed and read. Returns the number of bytes written, or a negative error number. A short count is
ordinary and the rest has to be written by calling again.
`buffer` must be readable for `count` bytes.
doc.returns: the bytes written, or a negative error number

doc.summary: Closes `fd` and releases what the kernel held for it.
doc.markdown:
Closes `fd` and releases what the kernel held for it.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. A failure does not mean the descriptor is still open, so retrying a
failed close can close one another thread has since opened under the same number.
doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.markdown:
`AT_FDCWD`: resolve a relative path against the current directory rather than a descriptor.
FreeBSD spells this `-100`, the same value Linux uses, which is one of the few places the two agree exactly.

doc.markdown: `O_RDONLY`: open for reading only.

doc.summary: `O_WRONLY`: open for writing only.

doc.markdown: `O_RDWR`: open for both reading and writing.

doc.markdown:

value must never be carried between the two packages.

items.name: OpenAt
items.signature: pub func OpenAt(directoryFd: FileDescriptor, path: *char8, flags: int32, mode: FileMode) -> int64

doc.summary: Opens `path` relative to `directoryFd` and returns a descriptor, or a negative error number.
doc.markdown:
Opens `path` relative to `directoryFd` and returns a descriptor, or a negative error number.
`directoryFd` is `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path. `mode` is read only when `OpenCreate` is set.
`path` must be non-null and terminated. The mode is masked by the process umask.

params.name: directoryFd
params.markdown: the directory `path` is relative to, or `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path

params.name: path
params.markdown: the path to open, as a null-terminated byte string

params.name: flags
params.markdown: the access mode and the open flags, combined with `|`

params.name: mode
params.markdown: the permission bits for a file this creates, ignored otherwise

doc.returns: the new descriptor, or a negative error number

items.name: Lseek
items.signature: pub func Lseek(fd: FileDescriptor, offset: FileOffset, whence: int32) -> int64

doc.summary: Moves the file offset of `fd` and returns where it ended up, or a negative error number.
doc.markdown:
Moves the file offset of `fd` and returns where it ended up, or a negative error number.
Seeking past the end creates a hole when something is later written there. A pipe reports `ESPIPE`.

params.name: offset
params.markdown: how far to move, interpreted according to `whence`

doc.returns: the resulting offset from the start, or a negative error number

items.name: Getcwd
items.signature: pub func Getcwd(buffer: *var char8, size: uint) -> int64

doc.summary: Writes the current working directory's absolute path into `buffer`, NUL-terminated.
doc.markdown:
Writes the current working directory's absolute path into `buffer`, NUL-terminated.
Returns zero, or a negative error number — unlike Linux's, which returns the length. `ERANGE` where the
buffer is too small for the answer.
`buffer` must be writable for `size` bytes.

params.name: buffer
params.markdown: receives the working directory as a null-terminated path

doc.returns: the bytes written including the terminator, or a negative error number

doc.summary: Makes `path` the process's working directory.
doc.markdown:
Makes `path` the process's working directory.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. The change is process-wide and immediately visible to every thread.
doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

items.name: ReadlinkAt
items.signature: pub func ReadlinkAt(directoryFd: FileDescriptor, path: *char8, buffer: *var char8, size: uint) -> int64

doc.summary: Reads the text a symbolic link holds into `buffer`.
doc.markdown:
Reads the text a symbolic link holds into `buffer`.
`directoryFd` is `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path. Returns the number of bytes written, or a negative error
number. The text is **not** NUL-terminated, and is silently truncated where it does not fit.

params.name: directoryFd
params.markdown: the directory `path` is relative to, or `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path

params.name: buffer
params.markdown: receives the link's text, without a terminator

doc.returns: the bytes written, which equals `size` when the text was truncated, or a negative error number

doc.summary: `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`: act on a symbolic link itself rather than on what it points at.
doc.markdown: `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`: act on a symbolic link itself rather than on what it points at.

Fills `statBuffer` with what the kernel knows about the file `path` names.
`directoryFd` is `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path. `flags` is zero to follow a symbolic link at the end of the

items.signature: pub func FchmodAt(directoryFd: FileDescriptor, path: *char8, mode: FileMode, flags: int32) -> int64

doc.markdown:
Sets the permission bits of the file `path` names.
`directoryFd` is `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path. `flags` may carry `SymlinkNoFollow`. Returns zero, or a

items.signature: pub func UtimensAt(directoryFd: FileDescriptor, path: *char8, times: *opaque, flags: int32) -> int64

doc.markdown:
Sets the access and modification times of the file `path` names.

params.markdown: the directory `path` is relative to, or `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path

params.markdown: the path whose times are set

params.name: flags
params.markdown: zero to follow a final symbolic link, or `SymlinkNoFollow`

Creates a hard link: `newPath` becomes a second name for the file `oldPath` names.

items.name: SymlinkAt
items.signature: pub func SymlinkAt(target: *char8, newDirectoryFd: FileDescriptor, linkPath: *char8) -> int64

doc.summary: Creates a symbolic link at `linkPath` holding `target` as its text.
doc.markdown:
Creates a symbolic link at `linkPath` holding `target` as its text.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. The target is stored, not checked: a dangling link is created as
readily as a good one, which is a property callers rely on.

params.name: target

items.name: Getdirentries
items.signature: pub func Getdirentries(fd: FileDescriptor, buffer: *var opaque, count: uint, position: *var int64) -> int64

doc.summary: Reads directory entries from `fd` into `buffer`.
doc.markdown:
Reads directory entries from `fd` into `buffer`.
The buffer holds packed `dirent` records: the file number at offset 0 (8 bytes), a seek cookie at 8 (8 bytes),
the record's length at 16 (2 bytes), the entry type at 18 (1 byte), padding at 19, the name's length at 20
(2 bytes), padding at 22, and the name from 24. The kernel writes as many whole records as fit.
The fourth parameter is named as macOS names `Getdirentries64`'s, which is the same output.
`buffer` must be writable for `count` bytes, and `position` must be null or writable for an `int64`.

params.name: position
params.markdown: receives the position of the block read, and may be null

doc.returns: the bytes filled, zero at the end of the directory, or a negative error number

doc.summary: Flushes everything written to `fd` through to the storage device.
doc.markdown:
Flushes everything written to `fd` through to the storage device.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. Without it, data a successful `Write` reported may still be lost.
doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

items.signature: pub func Ftruncate(fd: FileDescriptor, length: FileOffset) -> int64

doc.summary: Sets the length of the file behind `fd` to `length`.
doc.markdown:
Sets the length of the file behind `fd` to `length`.
Growing creates a hole rather than allocating, so a later write into it can still fail with `ENOSPC`.

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.markdown:
Removes the name `path` from its directory.
`flags` is zero for a file or `RemoveDirectory` for an empty directory. Removing a name does not free the file:
anything still holding it open keeps using it.
`path` must be non-null and terminated.

params.name: directoryFd
params.markdown: the directory `path` is relative to, or `AtFdCwd` for an ordinary path

params.name: flags
params.markdown: zero for a file, or `RemoveDirectory` for a directory

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

Reports `EEXIST` when the name is taken, which is how this is used as a lock.

doc.summary: Renames `oldPath` to `newPath`, each resolved against its own directory descriptor.
doc.markdown:
Renames `oldPath` to `newPath`, each resolved against its own directory descriptor.
Within one file system this replaces any existing `newPath` atomically. Across file systems it reports `EXDEV`

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

items.name: Fstat
items.signature: pub func Fstat(fd: FileDescriptor, statBuffer: *var opaque) -> int64

doc.summary: Fills `statBuffer` with what the kernel knows about the file behind `fd`.
doc.markdown:
Fills `statBuffer` with what the kernel knows about the file behind `fd`.
The kernel's `struct stat` is not modelled here: its layout is FreeBSD's own and differs from Linux's in both
size and field order.
`statBuffer` must be writable for the whole of FreeBSD's `struct stat`, which this does not check.
doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

items.name: Dup2
items.signature: pub func Dup2(oldFd: FileDescriptor, newFd: FileDescriptor) -> int64

doc.summary: Makes `newFd` a copy of `oldFd`, closing whatever `newFd` was.
doc.markdown:
Makes `newFd` a copy of `oldFd`, closing whatever `newFd` was.
Returns `newFd`, or a negative error number. Duplicating a descriptor onto itself returns it unchanged.
FreeBSD has `dup2` on both architectures, so this is the plain form rather than Linux's `dup3`; setting
close-on-exec is a separate `fcntl` this package does not wrap.

params.name: newFd
params.markdown: the number the duplicate should have

doc.returns: `newFd`, or a negative error number

items.name: Pipe2
items.signature: pub func Pipe2(descriptors: *var int32, flags: int32) -> int64

doc.summary: Creates a pipe and writes its two descriptors into `descriptors`.
doc.markdown:
Creates a pipe and writes its two descriptors into `descriptors`.
The reading end lands at index zero and the writing end at index one. `flags` may carry `OpenCloseOnExec` and
`OpenNonBlocking`.
`descriptors` must be writable for two `int32` values.

params.name: descriptors
params.markdown: receives the read end at index zero and the write end at index one

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.summary: `PROT_NONE`: the pages may not be touched at all.
doc.markdown: `PROT_NONE`: the pages may not be touched at all.

doc.summary: `PROT_READ`: the pages may be read.
doc.markdown: `PROT_READ`: the pages may be read.

doc.summary: `PROT_WRITE`: the pages may be written.
doc.markdown: `PROT_WRITE`: the pages may be written.

doc.summary: `PROT_EXEC`: the pages may be executed.
doc.markdown: `PROT_EXEC`: the pages may be executed.

doc.summary: `MAP_SHARED`: writes are visible to other mappings of the same object and reach it.
doc.markdown: `MAP_SHARED`: writes are visible to other mappings of the same object and reach it.

doc.summary: `MAP_PRIVATE`: writes are private to this mapping and never reach the object.
doc.markdown: `MAP_PRIVATE`: writes are private to this mapping and never reach the object.

doc.summary: `MAP_FIXED`: place the mapping exactly at the requested address, replacing whatever was there.
doc.markdown: `MAP_FIXED`: place the mapping exactly at the requested address, replacing whatever was there.

doc.summary: `MAP_EXCL`: with `MapFixed`, refuse the address rather than replace what occupies it.
doc.markdown:
`MAP_EXCL`: with `MapFixed`, refuse the address rather than replace what occupies it.
The one way to ask whether a range is free: a fixed, exclusive request over anything already mapped fails with
`ENOMEM`, and one over a hole takes it. `Mprotect` cannot answer that question, since it skips the holes in a
range rather than refusing them.

doc.summary: `MAP_ANON`: the mapping is backed by zeroed pages rather than by a file.
doc.markdown:
`MAP_ANON`: the mapping is backed by zeroed pages rather than by a file.
FreeBSD numbers this differently from Linux, which is one of the reasons the two packages are separate.

items.name: Mmap
items.signature: pub func Mmap(address: *opaque, length: uint, protection: int32, flags: int32, fd: int32, offset: uint64) -> int64

doc.summary: Creates a mapping and returns its address, or a negative error number.
doc.markdown:
Creates a mapping and returns its address, or a negative error number.
`address` is a hint unless `MapFixed` is set. `fd` is the object to map, or `-1` with `MapAnonymous`. Testing the
result needs `Errors::IsError` rather than a sign test, since a valid address may have its top bit set.
`MapFixed` replaces whatever occupies the address, including a mapping this program depends on, unless
`MapExclusive` is set with it.

params.name: address
params.markdown: a hint for where to map, or null to let the kernel choose

params.name: length
params.markdown: how many bytes, rounded up to whole pages

params.name: protection
params.markdown: what may be done with the pages, as `Protection*` flags

params.name: fd
params.markdown: the file to map, or -1 with `MapAnonymous`

params.name: offset
params.markdown: where in the file the mapping starts

doc.returns: the mapping's address, or a negative error number

items.name: Munmap
items.signature: pub func Munmap(address: *opaque, length: uint) -> int64

doc.summary: Releases the mapping that begins at `address` and spans `length` bytes.
doc.markdown:
Releases the mapping that begins at `address` and spans `length` bytes.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. Releasing a range that was never mapped succeeds and does nothing.
Every pointer into the range becomes invalid.

params.name: address
params.markdown: a page-aligned address to release from

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.summary: Sets the program break and returns where it ended up.
doc.markdown:
Sets the program break and returns where it ended up.
Reports failure by not moving rather than by an error number. The break is a single process-wide value.

params.name: address
params.markdown: where to move the program break, or null to read it

doc.returns: the resulting break, or a negative error number

doc.summary: `MADV_NORMAL`: no advice; the default.
doc.markdown: `MADV_NORMAL`: no advice; the default.

doc.summary: `MADV_RANDOM`: the pages will be touched in no useful order.
doc.markdown: `MADV_RANDOM`: the pages will be touched in no useful order.

doc.summary: `MADV_SEQUENTIAL`: the pages will be touched in order.
doc.markdown: `MADV_SEQUENTIAL`: the pages will be touched in order.

doc.summary: `MADV_WILLNEED`: the pages will be read soon.
doc.markdown: `MADV_WILLNEED`: the pages will be read soon.

doc.summary: `MADV_DONTNEED`: the pages are not needed soon.
doc.markdown:
`MADV_DONTNEED`: the pages are not needed soon.
FreeBSD's meaning is weaker than Linux's: it does not discard the pages, so an anonymous page does not read back
as zero afterwards. `MADV_FREE` is the one that lets the kernel take the storage, and that difference is exactly
why an advice value must not be carried between the two packages.

doc.summary: `MADV_FREE`: the pages may be reclaimed, and read back as zero if they are.
doc.markdown: `MADV_FREE`: the pages may be reclaimed, and read back as zero if they are.

items.name: Mprotect
items.signature: pub func Mprotect(address: *opaque, length: uint, protection: int32) -> int64

doc.summary: Changes what may be done with the pages covering a range.
doc.markdown:
Changes what may be done with the pages covering a range.
`address` must be page-aligned. Returns zero, or a negative error number. Removing a permission takes effect at
once, so a thread touching the range concurrently faults.
Nothing checks that the range was ever mapped, and a hardened system refuses writable executable memory.

params.name: length
params.markdown: how many bytes, rounded up to whole pages

params.name: protection
params.markdown: what may be done with them afterwards

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

items.name: Madvise
items.signature: pub func Madvise(address: *opaque, length: uint, advice: int32) -> int64

doc.summary: Tells the kernel how the pages covering a range are about to be used.
doc.markdown:
Tells the kernel how the pages covering a range are about to be used.
Advice is advice: the kernel is free to ignore it. `AdviseFree` is the one that actually releases storage.
`AdviseFree` loses whatever the range held.

params.name: length
params.markdown: how many bytes the advice covers

doc.returns: zero, or a negative error number

doc.summary: `CTL_HW`: the sysctl branch describing the machine.
doc.markdown: `CTL_HW`: the sysctl branch describing the machine.

doc.summary: `HW_PAGESIZE`: the leaf under `CtlHardware` holding the page size, in bytes.
doc.markdown: `HW_PAGESIZE`: the leaf under `CtlHardware` holding the page size, in bytes.

doc.summary: The size of a page, asked of the kernel.
doc.markdown:
The size of a page, asked of the kernel.
FreeBSD publishes this as the `hw.pagesize` sysctl rather than as a dedicated call, and that is the query this
package uses: it needs no libc, no auxiliary vector and no state captured at process start. The value is a
power of two and is the granularity `Mmap` rounds to.
A caller that cannot use a failure has no business asking: the whole point of returning one is that a system
which will not answer is not a system to guess about.
doc.returns: the page size in bytes, or a negative error number

doc.summary: Ends the calling process with `code`.
doc.markdown:
Ends the calling process with `code`.
Only the low eight bits reach a waiting parent. Does not return, and nothing is flushed or destroyed on the way
out.

Widens a file descriptor to the register width a system call takes it in.
